extracted.intended_audience: CJR-X participants (hospitals), CJR-X collaborators (ACOs, PGPs, NPPGPs, TGPs, physicians), collaboration agents/downstream agents, and legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and program safeguards for CJR‑X sharing arrangements, gainsharing/alignment/distribution/downstream payments, documentation, beneficiary incentives, enforcement, and fraud-and-abuse waivers. Targets participants, collaborators, collaboration agents, and downstream collaboration agents in the CJR‑X model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gainsharing payment methodology must be based solely on quality and CJR‑X activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of any gainsharing payments must be determined in accordance with a methodology that is solely based on quality of care and the provision of CJR‑X activities and must not be conditioned on the volume or value of referrals or business generated by or among parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considered but rejected methodologies that take into account volume/value of referrals or business. The methodology should align gainsharing directly with model goals (quality and CJR‑X activities). Comments sought on flexibility to account for amount of CJR‑X activities provided by a collaborator relative to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate gainsharing/distribution payment cap relative to reconciliation/gainsharing amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: For each performance year, the aggregate amount of all gainsharing payments derived from a reconciliation payment amount by the CJR‑X participant must not exceed the amount of the reconciliation payment amount. For distribution payments, total distribution payments in a performance year must not exceed the gainsharing payment received by the CJR‑X collaborator for that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures payments distributed do not exceed the underlying funds available from reconciliation/gainsharing and prevents over‑distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conditioning payments on referrals or business volume
rubrics_metrics.description: No entity or individual may condition the opportunity to make or receive gainsharing payments, alignment payments, distribution payments, downstream distribution payments, or similar arrangements on the volume or value of referrals or business otherwise generated by, between, or among participants, collaborators, collaboration agents, downstream collaboration agents, or affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit safeguard against inducements tied to referral volume/value; applies both directly and indirectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for noncompliance and recoupment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR‑X participant must not make a gainsharing payment to a CJR‑X collaborator that is subject to any action for noncompliance by CMS or any other federal or state entity or subject to noncompliance with any other federal or state laws or regulations, or for provision of substandard care or other integrity problems. The sharing arrangement must require recovery of any gainsharing payment that contained funds derived from a CMS overpayment on a reconciliation payment amount or was based on the submission of false or fraudulent data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides program integrity safeguards; arrangements must include recoupment mechanisms and bar payments tied to regulatory noncompliance or fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and payment traceability standards (GAAP / Yellow Book / traceable cash)
rubrics_metrics.description: All gainsharing payments and any alignment, distribution, or downstream distribution payments must be administered by the CJR‑X participant (or CJR‑X collaborator as applicable) in accordance with GAAP and Government Auditing Standards (The Yellow Book). All such payments must be made by check, electronic funds transfer, or another traceable cash transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal intended to mitigate administrative burden of strict EFT requirement for small suppliers while ensuring traceability; comments sought on administrative impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment payments: timing and eligibility restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment payments from a CJR‑X collaborator to a CJR‑X participant may be made at any interval agreed by both parties but must not be issued, distributed, or paid prior to CMS calculation of the repayment amount, and cannot be assessed in the absence of a repayment amount. The CJR‑X participant must not receive amounts under a sharing arrangement that are not alignment payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures alignment payments are tied to CMS‑determined repayment amounts and avoids advance/untied payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment payment aggregate limits and participant retention of repayment responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For a performance year, the aggregate amount of all alignment payments received by the CJR‑X participant from all collaborators must not exceed 50 percent of the repayment amount. Aggregate alignment payments from a single collaborator that is not an ACO may not be greater than 25 percent of the participant's repayment amount; from a collaborator that is an ACO may not be greater than 50 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits ensure CJR‑X participant retains significant responsibility for repayment and prevents excessive shifting of repayment burden to collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements for sharing arrangements (contemporaneous documentation, lists, public reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants must: document the sharing arrangement contemporaneously with establishment; maintain accurate current and historical lists of all CJR‑X collaborators (names/addresses), update such lists at least quarterly, and publicly report current/historical lists on the participant's website; and require contemporaneous documentation by each collaborator for any gainsharing/alignment payment including nature of payment, parties, date, amount, date/amount of any recoupment, and explanation for recoupment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires retention and provision of access to documentation per §512.135 and 42 CFR 1001.952(ii). These measures are program integrity safeguards and CMS seeks comment on additional or different safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records and systems documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants must keep records for: processes to determine/verify collaborator Medicare eligibility (if Medicare‑enrolled); a plan to track internal cost savings; information on accounting systems used to track internal cost savings; a description of health information technology used to track reconciliation/repayment/internal savings; and a plan to track gainsharing and alignment payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must be retained and provided access to in accordance with §512.135 and related regs; supports transparency and auditability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution arrangements: definitions and sole-purpose standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'collaboration agent', 'distribution arrangement', and 'distribution payment'. A 'distribution arrangement' is a financial arrangement between a CJR‑X collaborator that is a PGP, NPPGP, or TGP and a collaboration agent for the sole purpose of sharing a gainsharing payment received by the PGP/NPPGP/TGP. The amount of distribution payments must be determined in accordance with a methodology that is solely based on quality of care and the provision of CJR‑X activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors gainsharing methodology constraint to ensure distribution aligns with quality and CJR‑X activities. CMS sought comments on definitions and whether greater flexibility is needed for PGP/NPPGP/TGP member payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution arrangement formalities and voluntariness
rubrics_metrics.description: All distribution arrangements must be in writing and signed by parties, contain an effective date, and be entered into before care is furnished to CJR‑X beneficiaries under the arrangement. Participation must be voluntary and without penalty for nonparticipation, and the arrangement must require the collaboration agent to comply with all applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures arrangements are documented, prospective, voluntary, and legally compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution payment eligibility tied to direct patient care during performance year
rubrics_metrics.description: A collaboration agent is eligible to receive a distribution payment only if the collaboration agent furnished or billed for an item or service rendered to a beneficiary during an episode that occurred during the same performance year for which the CJR‑X participant accrued the internal cost savings or earned the reconciliation/gainsharing amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguard against payments unrelated to direct care for CJR‑X beneficiaries in the performance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution payment limits, clinical independence, and prohibition on inducing under/over‑treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Total distribution payments in a performance year must not exceed the gainsharing payment received by the CJR‑X collaborator; collaboration agents must retain ability to make decisions in the best interests of beneficiaries (device/supply/treatment selection); distribution arrangements must not induce reduction/limitation of medically necessary items/services or reward medically unnecessary services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects beneficiary care and prevents financial incentives from distorting clinical decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution arrangement documentation and prohibitions on multiple parallel arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X collaborators must maintain contemporaneous documentation including written agreements, date/amount of any distribution payment(s), identity of each collaboration agent receiving payments, and a description of the methodology and accounting formula for determining amounts. A CJR‑X collaborator may not enter into a distribution arrangement with any individual/entity that has a sharing arrangement with the same CJR‑X participant to avoid duplicate counting and exceeding payment limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents duplicate counting of contributions and preserves limits on absolute dollars to individuals/entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream distribution arrangements: definitions and sole‑purpose standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'downstream collaboration agent', 'downstream distribution arrangement', and 'downstream distribution payment'. A downstream distribution arrangement is a financial arrangement between a collaboration agent that is both a PGP/NPPGP/TGP and an ACO participant and a downstream collaboration agent for the sole purpose of sharing a distribution payment received by the PGP/NPPGP/TGP. Amounts (e.g., from NPPGP to NPPGP member or TGP to TGP member) must be determined in accordance with a methodology solely based on quality of care and provision of CJR‑X activities and may take into account relative amounts of CJR‑X activities provided by downstream agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows valuation based on relative contributions to CJR‑X activities among downstream agents while maintaining quality‑based methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream distribution formalities, eligibility, and payment caps
rubrics_metrics.description: All downstream distribution arrangements must be in writing, signed, entered before care furnished, voluntary, and require compliance with laws. Downstream collaboration agents are eligible only if the PGP billed for an item/service furnished by the downstream agent to a CJR‑X beneficiary during an episode attributed to the same performance year. Total downstream distribution payments to downstream agents must not exceed the distribution payment received by the collaboration agent; payments must be traceable cash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors requirements for distribution arrangements to ensure alignment with care rendered in the same performance year and prevent over‑distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream distribution protections for clinical independence and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Downstream distribution arrangements must preserve the downstream agent's ability to make decisions in the best interests of the patient; must not induce reductions in medically necessary care or reward unnecessary services. PGP/NPPGP/TGP must maintain contemporaneous documentation: written agreements, date/amount of payments, identity of downstream agents who received payments, and description of methodology/accounting formula. PGP/NPPGP/TGP may not enter into downstream arrangements with members who have a sharing arrangement with a CJR‑X participant or distribution arrangement with the same ACO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents duplicate counting and overpayment across multiple arrangement types and preserves audit trail and beneficiary protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary engagement incentives: general conditions and connection to clinical care
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants may provide in‑kind patient engagement incentives (including items of technology) to beneficiaries in an episode if: the incentive is provided directly by the participant or by an agent under their direction and control during an episode; the item/service is reasonably connected to the beneficiary's medical care; and it is a preventive care item/service or advances a clinical goal by engaging the beneficiary in managing their health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed to be consistent with anti‑kickback statute safe harbor for CMS‑sponsored model patient incentives (42 CFR 1001.952(ii)) if requirements are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology incentives: value thresholds, minimum‑necessary, and retrieval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Items/services involving technology provided to a beneficiary may not exceed $1,000 in retail value per beneficiary per episode and must be the minimum necessary to advance a clinical goal. For items exceeding $75 in retail value, the item remains the property of the CJR‑X participant and must be retrieved at the end of the episode; the participant must document all retrieval attempts and reasons why retrieval was not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhanced safeguards for higher‑value technology to prevent misuse; documentation of diligent, good faith retrieval attempts can satisfy retrieval requirement when physical retrieval is impossible (e.g., beneficiary died or moved).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation thresholds for beneficiary incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants must maintain contemporaneous documentation of items/services furnished as beneficiary engagement incentives that exceed $25 in retail value, including date provided, the incentive and estimated value, and identity of the beneficiary. For technology items > $75, documentation must also include contemporaneous documentation of any attempt to retrieve the technology and follow‑up steps if misappropriated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must be retained and provided in accordance with §512.135; CMS seeks comment on financial thresholds and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible clinical goals for beneficiary incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiary incentives must advance one of the following clinical goals of CJR‑X: beneficiary adherence to drug regimens; beneficiary adherence to a care plan; reduction of readmissions and complications resulting from treatment during the episode; management of chronic diseases and conditions affected by the episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentives should be closely related to provision of high‑quality care and not serve as inducements to seek care from specific providers; similar to CJR Model guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement authority not limited by model provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: OIG authority and authority of other Government agencies to audit, evaluate, investigate, or inspect CJR‑X participants, collaborators, collaboration agents, downstream agents, or any other person/entity or their records, data, or information is not limited or restricted by model provisions. Enforcement authority for CJR‑X would be in accordance with standard Innovation Center model provisions at §512.160.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model does not constrain investigative or audit powers of OIG or other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud and abuse waivers and CMS/OIG safe harbor expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1115A(d)(1) the Secretary may waive certain statutory requirements solely for testing models. No fraud/abuse waivers are being issued in this proposed rule; any waivers for CJR‑X would be separately documented and apply solely to CJR‑X. CMS expects to determine that the anti‑kickback statute safe harbor for CMS‑sponsored model arrangements and patient incentives (42 CFR 1001.952(ii)(1)/(2)) is available to protect remuneration exchanged pursuant to covered CJR‑X financial arrangements and beneficiary incentives, if the final rule is issued and arrangements comply with conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains prior CJR waiver history, scope limits of waivers, and that safe harbor applicability is expected but contingent on final rule and compliance; stakeholders should not assume waivers exist based on this proposal.
